title: Post-launch metrics dashboard spec — Benchmark Report campaign
content:
Owner: Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops)
Primary consumers: PMM (Soojin), Growth (Ben), SDR Ops (Grace), Sales leadership, Exec staff
Last updated: 2025-07-22

---

1) Purpose / what we are measuring

This spec defines:
- Which KPIs we will report for the Benchmark Report launch (traffic → signup/activation → demo requests → SQLs → pipeline)
- Required event instrumentation + naming conventions
- HubSpot campaign tagging rules to connect anonymous/known web activity to contacts, companies, and deals
- Definitions for “influenced pipeline” and the reporting views we will use post-launch

Non-goals:
- Perfect multi-touch attribution across all channels (we will implement pragmatic, auditable rules first)
- Building a long-lived “always-on” benchmark program dashboard (this is a post-launch measurement window with a refresh cadence)

Reporting window:
- Primary: Launch day through +6 weeks
- Secondary: +3 months roll-up (monthly)

---

2) KPI map (north stars + supporting metrics)

North-star outcomes (GTM):
A) Developer self-serve growth
- New signups attributed/influenced by benchmark assets
- Activation rate of those signups

B) Enterprise pipeline impact
- Demo requests and sales-qualified leads sourced by benchmark assets
- Influenced pipeline ($) and influenced closed-won ($)

Supporting: brand/awareness proxy signals
- Unique visitors, time on page, scroll depth, PDF downloads, webinar registrations/attendance


2.1 KPI definitions (plain English)

Traffic
- Sessions: visits to benchmark landing page and interactive table experience
- Unique visitors: deduplicated users by cookie/device (as defined by analytics tool)
- Source/medium: UTM-driven when available; fallback to referrer-based classification

Engagement (benchmark assets)
- Interactive engagement: any meaningful interaction with the benchmark table (filters, metric toggles, exports)
- Methodology engagement: click to methodology section / methodology page, dwell time threshold
- Asset consumption: PDF downloads, CSV/JSON exports

Conversions
- Hosted API signup: creation of a Redwood account (self-serve)
- Activated signup: first successful API call within 7 days of signup (definition below)
- Demo request: submission of enterprise/demo form (or “Contact sales” completion)

Pipeline
- Sourced pipeline: deals created where the first touch is benchmark campaign assets (strict rule)
- Influenced pipeline: deals created or progressed where benchmark campaign assets were touched within a defined lookback window (rule below)

---

3) Dashboard audiences + required views

We will build 3 reporting views:

(1) Exec summary (weekly)
- Topline traffic, conversion, pipeline impact
- Channel mix (community/social/email/partner/organic)
- Notable anomalies (bot traffic, incident-related drops, UTM gaps)

(2) Growth + PMM deep dive (daily during first 2 weeks, then weekly)
- Landing page + interactive table engagement by segment
- Funnel analysis: page → signup → activation
- A/B test performance for lifecycle email variants (if applicable)

(3) Sales/SDR view (weekly)
- Which accounts/contacts engaged with benchmark assets
- Engagement recency + intent signals (exports, methodology clicks)
- List exports to HubSpot views for sequences (subject to opt-in/permission)

Primary tooling assumption (current stack):
- Web analytics/events: Redwood product analytics (Segment-like capture) → warehouse + BI
- CRM: HubSpot for contacts/companies/deals + campaign association
- BI: Looker (or equivalent) pulling from warehouse + HubSpot sync

Note: If we cannot reliably join anonymous web IDs to HubSpot contacts, we still report aggregate web performance and only show influenced pipeline for “known” contacts.

---

4) Event taxonomy + required properties

We must support both:
- Anonymous measurement (UTMs, referrers)
- Known-user joins once the visitor signs up / submits a form

4.1 Canonical campaign metadata fields (attach to ALL benchmark-related events when available)

Required fields:
- campaign_name: "benchmark-report-2025"
- campaign_asset: e.g., "landing-page", "interactive-table", "pdf", "webinar", "blog"
- campaign_variant: e.g., "email-a", "email-b", "partner-x", "paid-social-1" (nullable)
- utm_source
- utm_medium
- utm_campaign
- utm_content (optional)
- utm_term (optional)
- referrer_domain (fallback)
- region (geo)
- device_type

Identity fields:
- anonymous_id (cookie/device)
- user_id (Redwood user id; set post-signup)
- account_id (Redwood account/workspace id; set post-signup)
- hubspotutk (if present)

4.2 Benchmark page interaction events (minimum set)

Event: benchmark_page_view
- Trigger: landing page view OR interactive table page view
- Properties: page_path, page_type ("landing"|"interactive"), content_version, experiment_id (if any)

Event: benchmark_table_filter_changed
- Trigger: user changes any filter
- Properties: filter_name (model|region|context_length|concurrency|metric), filter_value, previous_value

Event: benchmark_metric_toggled
- Trigger: toggle between latency/$ vs raw latency vs cost metrics
- Properties: metric_name

Event: benchmark_export_clicked
- Trigger: export action
- Properties: export_type ("csv"|"json"|"pdf"), export_scope ("current_view"|"all"), schema_version

Event: benchmark_cta_clicked
- Trigger: clicks primary CTA
- Properties: cta_type ("start-free"|"contact-sales"|"get-dedicated-sizing"|"read-methodology"), cta_location (hero|mid|footer|table)

Event: benchmark_methodology_link_clicked
- Trigger: click into methodology content
- Properties: destination ("on-page"|"methodology-page"|"github"), anchor_id (if applicable)

Event: benchmark_webinar_registered
- Trigger: registration confirmation
- Properties: webinar_id, source_asset

Event: benchmark_form_submitted
- Trigger: enterprise/demo form submit from benchmark context
- Properties: form_id, form_type (demo|contact|enterprise), company_size_bucket (if captured)

4.3 Conversion events (downstream)

Event: signup_completed
- Trigger: account created
- Properties: signup_source (derived), plan_type (trial|paid), email_domain_type (work|personal)

Event: activation_first_api_call
- Trigger: first successful API call for the account
- Properties: api_surface (chat|completions|embeddings|rerank), model_family, time_to_first_call_seconds

Definition: “Activated signup”
- activation_first_api_call within 7 days of signup_completed
- Exclusions: internal/test accounts; known bot domains

---

5) Traffic source classification (UTM + fallback)

We will categorize sessions into channels using this precedence:

(1) Explicit UTMs (preferred)
- utm_medium = email → Channel: Email
- utm_medium = social OR source in {x, twitter, linkedin} → Social
- utm_medium = partner → Partner
- utm_medium = community OR source in {hn, reddit} → Community
- utm_medium = paid → Paid

(2) Referrer-based fallback
- referrer_domain contains "t.co" / "twitter.com" → Social
- "linkedin.com" → Social
- "news.ycombinator.com" → Community
- "reddit.com" → Community
- otherwise "direct/none" → Direct
- otherwise → Referral

(3) Organic search
- referrer indicates major search engines and no UTMs → Organic Search

We will maintain a small mapping table (Marketing Ops-owned) with known partner domains and newsletter referrers.

---

6) HubSpot attribution + campaign tagging

6.1 HubSpot objects & fields we will rely on

Contact
- email
- original source / original source drill-down (HubSpot standard)
- latest source (HubSpot standard)
- campaign association (HubSpot campaigns)
- custom: last_benchmark_engagement_at (datetime)
- custom: benchmark_engagement_level (enum: low|medium|high)

Company
- domain
- industry
- region
- custom: benchmark_account_engagement (rollup)

Deal
- amount
- stage
- create date
- close date
- associated contacts/companies
- custom: benchmark_influenced (boolean)
- custom: benchmark_influenced_reason (string)
- custom: benchmark_influenced_first_touch_at (datetime)
- custom: benchmark_influenced_last_touch_at (datetime)
- custom: benchmark_influenced_lookback_days (number)

6.2 Campaign tagging conventions

We will create a HubSpot campaign:
- Campaign name: "Benchmark Report 2025"
- Internal key: benchmark-report-2025

Rules for associating activities to the campaign:
- Any form submission on benchmark landing page (or pages with utm_campaign=benchmark-report-2025) is associated to campaign
- Any webinar registration for the benchmark webinar is associated to campaign
- Any contact created from signup where first session has utm_campaign=benchmark-report-2025 is associated to campaign

Engineering requirement:
- Ensure benchmark forms pass UTMs into HubSpot hidden fields
- Ensure the site preserves UTMs across navigation to signup where possible (or stores first-touch UTMs server-side)

6.3 Joining web events → HubSpot contacts

Order of operations:
1) If user submits a HubSpot form, HubSpot can associate the submission with contact + hubspotutk
2) If user signs up, Redwood app sets user_id/account_id; we store first-touch campaign metadata on the user/account
3) Warehouse job joins:
   - known contact email ↔ Redwood user email
   - Redwood account ↔ HubSpot company via domain matching (with exceptions list)

Limitations:
- Anonymous visitors who never convert cannot be tied to HubSpot; we report aggregate web performance separately.
- Domain matching can be noisy (subsidiaries, shared IT domains); require a small exceptions list maintained by RevOps.

---

7) Influenced pipeline: definitions and rules

We will report BOTH “Sourced” and “Influenced” so we can be honest about what the benchmark directly created vs assisted.

7.1 Sourced pipeline (strict)
A deal is “Benchmark-sourced” if:
- Deal create date is within reporting window AND
- The earliest known touch for the primary associated contact has utm_campaign=benchmark-report-2025 OR a benchmark campaign-associated form submission AND
- There is no earlier recorded touch for that contact in the prior 90 days that is attributed to another campaign.

If the above cannot be validated due to missing identity linkage, the deal is NOT counted as sourced.

7.2 Influenced pipeline (pragmatic)
A deal is “Benchmark-influenced” if:
- Deal is created any time within reporting window (or progresses stage within reporting window; see note) AND
- Any associated contact has at least one benchmark campaign touch within the lookback window prior to the deal create date

Lookback window (default): 45 days
- Rationale: matches typical cycle for early-stage Dedicated/Private evaluation triggered by a technical artifact

Benchmark campaign touch includes any of:
- benchmark_form_submitted
- benchmark_webinar_registered
- benchmark_export_clicked (csv/json/pdf)
- benchmark_cta_clicked (contact sales / dedicated sizing)
- benchmark_page_view with engagement threshold (see below)

Engagement threshold for page view counting as “touch”:
- At least 30s on page OR scroll depth ≥ 50% OR ≥ 2 benchmark_table_filter_changed events in a session

Deal-stage influence (optional add-on)
We may also flag “Benchmark influenced (stage)” if:
- Touch occurs AFTER deal creation but BEFORE SQL stage change
This helps Sales Enablement understand the report as late-stage collateral.

7.3 Deduping + counting rules
- Pipeline is counted once per deal (not per contact)
- If multiple associated contacts have touches, we use earliest_touch_at and latest_touch_at across all associated contacts
- If a deal is both sourced and influenced, count it under sourced only (and still mark influenced=true for drill-down)

7.4 Auditability requirements
For any influenced deal we should be able to show:
- Deal id, associated contact(s)
- Touch type(s), timestamp(s)
- Link/asset when applicable (e.g., export type)

---

8) Data model / warehouse tables (conceptual)

NOTE: this section is descriptive; implementation may vary.

Event table: analytics_events
- event_name
- occurred_at
- anonymous_id
- user_id
- account_id
- properties_json (raw)
- utm_* fields extracted columns

Dimension tables:
- dim_user (user_id, email, created_at, first_touch_utm_campaign, ...)
- dim_account (account_id, domain, plan_type, ...)
- hubspot_contacts (contact_id, email, company_id, campaign_associations, ...)
- hubspot_deals (deal_id, amount, stage, created_at, close_at, associated_contact_ids, ...)

Bridge table:
- bridge_user_contact (user_id ↔ contact_id, confidence score)

Derived mart:
- mart_benchmark_funnel_daily (date, channel, sessions, engagement, signups, activations, demo_requests)
- mart_benchmark_pipeline (deal_id, benchmark_sourced, benchmark_influenced, influenced_first_touch_at, influenced_last_touch_at, amount)

---

9) Dashboard tiles (exact requirements)

9.1 Exec summary
- Total benchmark sessions (weekly) + WoW change
- % sessions by channel (stacked)
- Engagement rate (interactive engagement / sessions)
- PDF download count
- Signups attributed to benchmark (first-touch)
- Activated signups (7-day)
- Demo requests from benchmark context
- Benchmark-sourced pipeline $ (sum of deal amount)
- Benchmark-influenced pipeline $ (sum of deal amount)
- Influenced closed-won $ (if any)

9.2 Growth/PMM deep dive
- Session → engagement → signup → activation funnel (overall + by channel)
- Time series: daily sessions + signups + demo requests
- Top entry pages (landing vs interactive deep links)
- Top CTAs clicked (start free vs contact sales vs methodology)
- Export behavior: csv vs json vs pdf; by channel; by geo
- Geo breakdown: NA/EU/APAC sessions and conversion rates
- Known data-quality flags: % sessions missing UTMs; spike detection

9.3 Sales/SDR view
- Account-level table:
  - Company, domain, region
  - Last benchmark touch date
  - Engagement level (low/med/high)
  - Touch types (export, webinar, form, methodology)
  - CTA clicked (if any)
  - Associated open deals + stage
- Contact-level list for routing (permissioned): name, email, company, last touch, recommended play (trial follow-up vs demo)

---

10) Data quality, exclusions, and caveats

Exclusions (must apply across dashboards):
- Internal Redwood traffic (office IPs, @redwoodinference.com users)
- Known bots/crawlers (UA-based + suspicious high-frequency patterns)
- QA/staging environments

Caveats to include on dashboards (small footnote):
- Attribution relies on UTMs and identity matching; some benchmark influence may be undercounted.
- Influenced pipeline is directional and should be interpreted alongside sourced pipeline.
- Deal amounts can change after creation; pipeline $ reflects latest known amount unless we snapshot.

Snapshot policy (recommended):
- Weekly snapshot of influenced pipeline amounts and stages to avoid retroactive drift.

---

11) Cadence + owners

Cadence
- Daily checks (first 10 business days): traffic + conversions + instrumentation sanity
- Weekly rollup: exec summary + pipeline review
- Week 6: final readout doc + learnings

Owners
- Web event instrumentation: Logan Wright (Engineering) with Felix Schneider (web)
- HubSpot fields/campaign setup: Isabelle Laurent (RevOps) + Tyler Benson (Mkt Ops)
- Warehouse marts + dashboards: Mei Lin (Data) + Tyler Benson
- Readout + narrative: Soojin Lee (PMM) + Ben Carter (Growth)

---

12) Open questions / decisions needed

1) BI tool of record for exec view (Looker vs HubSpot dashboard vs internal)
2) Deal amount snapshotting: do we snapshot weekly or use “current amount” only?
3) Lookback window for influenced pipeline: confirm 45 days vs 60 days
4) Whether post-deal-creation touches should count as influence (stage-based influence)
5) Permissioning for contact-level exports (Sales/SDR view)

Decision deadline: 2025-07-25 (so we can finalize dashboards before the post-launch retro)

---

13) Acceptance criteria (definition of done)

Instrumentation
- ≥ 95% of benchmark sessions have channel classification (UTM or fallback)
- CTA clicks and exports are captured and visible within 30 minutes

Dashboards
- Exec summary loads < 10s and is shareable weekly
- Growth view supports filtering by channel, geo, asset
- Pipeline mart shows sourced/influenced flags with drill-down touch evidence for each influenced deal

Ops
- A weekly email/slack summary is automated (or templated) and includes key caveats

---

Appendix A: Engagement level scoring (for Sales view)

Low
- Only benchmark_page_view with < 30s dwell and no interactions

Medium
- Any filter changes OR methodology click OR ≥ 50% scroll

High
- Any export (csv/json/pdf) OR webinar registration OR benchmark form submission OR contact-sales CTA click

Appendix B: Naming / page inventory (initial)
- /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar (landing)
- /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/table (interactive)
- /benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/methodology (methodology detail)

(Confirm final routes with Docs/Web before dashboard hard-coding.)
